subject: Re: Vendor fan-out impact on uptime accounting — Clarify maintenance attribution
messages:
From: Raj Patel <raj.patel@corecloud.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
Cc: contracts@corecloud.com
Date: 2026-10-06T08:12:00Z
Subject: Unexpected vendor maintenance cascade on 2026-10-05 — request for uptime recalc

Hi Soojin,

We're seeing a mismatch between our availability records and Redwood's uptime ledger for 2026-10-05 (window 03:40-04:30 UTC). CoreCloud performed an emergency maintenance step that day to patch an upstream peering provider, but our logs show the maintenance was targeted to a subset of POPs and should be classified as third-party maintenance under your SLA exception rules.

Can you confirm whether Redwood is counting the full 50-minute window as our responsibility? Attached is our maintenance bulletin and local POP fan-out logs (corecloud-maint-log-20261005.txt). If Redwood is including this in your uptime calculation, please re-run the attribution — the impact appears constrained to a failover path that your probes exercise but that our customers short-circuited.

We'd like to avoid an invoice dispute and would appreciate a quick reconciliation.

Thanks,
Raj Patel
SRE, CoreCloud
raj.patel@corecloud.com
+1 415-555-0199

Attachment: corecloud-maint-log-20261005.txt (text)

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-06T12:03:00Z
Subject: Re: Unexpected vendor maintenance cascade on 2026-10-05 — request for uptime recalc

Raj — thanks for the note and the log. We pulled the relevant telemetry and there are a couple of things I'd like to clarify before we recalculate: 

- Our edge probes registered elevated P95 latency and a partial routing flap starting at 03:36 UTC with a spike of 8% 5xx across three POPs, which persisted as intermittent errors until 04:25 UTC. That produced a detectable partial degradation by our SLO definition (see bullets below).
- The SLA guidance allows excluding "third-party scheduled maintenance" when the third party initiated a documented maintenance outage and the customer's traffic had observable alternate paths. From the materials you shared, it isn't immediately clear whether CoreCloud's maintenance was announced and whether the downstream routes used by Redwood were excluded.

Next steps from our side: 
- Ben, can you pull the raw probe traces and a 1-minute tokenized availability slice for 03:30–04:30 UTC and populate the CSV (I pasted it as redwood-uptime-slice-20261005.csv).
- Raj — please confirm whether CoreCloud published a customer-facing maintenance bulletin (time-stamped) and whether the affected POPs match the IPs in your attachment. If you have an internal RCA or a ticket ID, forward that.

If it turns out the event is a third-party scheduled maintenance that explicitly covered the routes we probe, we will exclude the minutes covered. If instead the event was an upstream failover that caused partial degradation on our side, we will need to apportion credit per the SLO's partial-degradation rules (section 3.2).

I'm looping Marissa for customer impact/context and Ben for the metric pull. We'll aim to have an updated ledger entry or proposed apportionment by end of day 10/07.

Regards,
Soojin Lee
Principal Reliability Manager
Redwood Inference
soojin_lee@redwood.ai
---
Attachment referenced: redwood-uptime-slice-20261005.csv (generated metric slice)

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-07T09:18:00Z
Subject: Re: Vendor fan-out impact on uptime accounting — internal metric summary

Quick internal summary of what I pulled for 03:30–04:30 UTC on 2026-10-05 (dashboard link: https://console.redwood.ai/dashboards/uptime/CC-3471/2026-10-05):

- Observed symptom: Partial degradation (elevated P95 latency + transient 5xx) across POPs A, B and C, starting 03:36 UTC, peak at 03:48–03:52 UTC, tapered off by 04:25 UTC.
- Probe coverage: Our synthetic probes hit the same upstream ASNs that CoreCloud references, but we also observed that 14% of traffic re-routed to fallback paths with acceptable latency — that suggests some customer flows used alternate routes.
- Accounting recommendation: Two-phase approach:
  1) Conservative exclusion: remove minutes where CoreCloud clearly documents scheduled maintenance and offers a route-exclusion statement.
  2) For residual minutes where partial degradation remained and CoreCloud's logs indicate transient failover rather than planned maintenance, apportion credit by percentage of impacted tokens (we measured ~6.7% token-level impact across the hour), capped per SLA formula.

Attached CSV contains per-minute availability, token counts and error buckets (redwood-uptime-slice-20261005.csv). My proposal for communication back to CoreCloud: a) list excluded minutes (if any) b) show the residual calculated credit with the apportionment math so it's transparent.

Marissa — if you agree, I'll draft the external reply and include the math + a suggested credit certificate.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.ai

Appreciate the quick turnaround and Ben's analysis. CoreCloud will: 
- Publish the customer-facing maintenance bulletin and a ticketed RCA by EOD tomorrow.
- Provide the ASN/POP mapping for the affected nodes so you can cross-walk IPs.
- If Redwood proceeds with an apportionment, we will accept the proposed approach but will ask our contracts team to review the credit computation. We'll circulate a DocuSign packet for the settlement.

For now, can Redwood produce the per-minute list you plan to exclude and the residual credit calculation so we have a starting point for contracts? If you can attach that as a CSV, that'll speed the DocuSign flow.

Thanks —
Raj
SRE, CoreCloud
raj.patel@corecloud.com
